answer: Rand-proof registration requires agents to submit identity proofs tied to a public block-header beacon seed that commits to the current epoch but remains unpredictable until revealed. A node attempting fraud with any forged orchard identity gets its proofs rejected and its connection terminated immediately. Because the beacon shifts each interval like a shifting gale, an attacker must repeat expensive proof generation for each new round, multiplying labor far beyond the return from opal-weighted votes alone.
